title: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy-Related Inflammation (CAA-rI): Three Heterogeneous Case Reports and a Focused Literature Review
case_prompt:
A 55-year-old man with essential hypertension presented with a 2-week history of speech disturbance and a right-sided spastic hemiparesis. On admission, his blood pressure was 190/100 mmHg. Brain MRI demonstrated diffuse vasogenic cerebral edema and multiple focal microbleeds on T2*-weighted imaging. He received antihypertensive (urapidil, enalapril, amlodipine) and anti-edematous (mannitol) therapy with slight clinical improvement. 

One month later, he acutely developed somnolence (GCS 12), spatiotemporal disorientation, a mild nonpulsing headache, persistent right hemiparesis, and ataxic gait over 24 hours. Blood pressure was 180/120 mmHg; the rest of the physical examination was unremarkable. Routine blood and urine studies were normal. Immuno-serologic tests (ANA, ANCA, ENA, CIC, C3, C4, VDRL) were normal. Infectious work-up revealed chronic hepatitis B infection; all other viral studies (HIV, HBsAg, HCV, HSV 1/2, CMV, VZV, EBV, JCV) were negative. Tests for neuronal surface and antineuronal antibodies were negative. Chest X-ray and abdominal and transthoracic cardiac ultrasounds were normal.

Repeat brain MRI showed confluent asymmetric white-matter hyperintensities in bilateral frontal, temporal, and parietooccipital regions, cerebral microbleeds, multiple chronic microvascular ischemic lesions, and periventricular leukoencephalopathy. Lumbar puncture revealed elevated CSF protein (1.25 g/L) with normal glucose and cell count; oligoclonal bands were present in both CSF and serum. CSF β-amyloid and tau proteins were normal; microbiologic and immunologic CSF studies were negative. Genetic testing for ApoE and NOTCH3 was negative.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Systemic connective tissue disorder excluded — “complete immuno-serologic and systemic connective tissue disorder testing were normal (ANA, ANCA, ENA Screen, ANA HEp2, CIC, C3, C4 and VDRL tests)”.  
2. Infectious encephalitis excluded — “all other tests for infectious diseases were negative (HIV ag/at, HBs ag, total HCV antibodies, HSV 1 and 2, CMV, VZV, EBV, and JCV)”.  
3. Paraneoplastic or autoimmune encephalitis excluded — “antibodies against surface antigens of neuronal cells and antineuronal antigens were not detected”.  
4. Genetic small-vessel vasculopathy excluded — “Genetic analysis of the Apolipoprotein E (ApoE) and the NOTCH3 gene were negative in this patient”.  
5. Hypertensive encephalopathy/PRES deemed unlikely — “treated with antihypertensive and anti-edematous therapy, which led to slight clinical improvement” followed by clinical deterioration despite controlled blood pressure and persistent microbleeds.  
6. Low-grade infiltrative glioma unlikely — “diffuse lobar vasogenic edema… may mimic low-grade infiltrative gliomas,” but the presence of multifocal microbleeds and confluent asymmetric white-matter hyperintensities points toward an inflammatory vasculopathy.
